```{python}
#| label: imports
import polars as pl
import altair as alt
from altair import datum
```

```{python}
#| label: plotting-function

def plot(df, part="preprocessing", shape_legend=True):
    base = (
        alt.Chart(df)
        .encode(x="sample", xOffset="version", fill="version")
        .transform_filter(datum.pipeline_part == part)
    )
    if not shape_legend:
        shape = alt.Shape("rule", legend=None)
    else:
        shape = alt.Shape("rule")

    runtime_points = base.mark_point(size=60, color="black", strokeWidth=0.5).encode(
        y="s", shape=shape, tooltip=["rule"]
    )
    runtime_bars = base.mark_bar().encode(y=alt.Y("sum(s):Q", title="Runtime (s)"))
    runtime = (runtime_bars + runtime_points).properties(title="Runtime")
    max_rss_points = (
        base.mark_point(size=60, color="black", strokeWidth=0.5)
        .encode(
            y=alt.Y("max_rss_gb", title="Peak RAM (GB)").scale(type="log"),
            shape=shape,
            tooltip=["rule"],
        )
        # .transform_calculate(max_rss="datum.max_rss / 1000")
        .properties(title="Memory (Peak)")
    )
    eff_points = base.mark_point(size=60, color="black", strokeWidth=0.5).encode(
        y="thread_eff", shape="rule", tooltip=["rule"]
    )
    eff_bars = base.mark_bar().encode(
        y=alt.Y("mean(thread_eff):Q", title="Thread efficiency")
    )
    eff = (eff_bars + eff_points).properties(title="Thread efficiency")
    mem_points = base.mark_point(size=60, color="black", strokeWidth=0.5).encode(
        y="GB_hours",
        shape=shape,
        tooltip=["rule"],
    )
    mem_bars = base.mark_bar().encode(
        y=alt.Y("sum(GB_hours):Q", title="GB-hours (Peak RAM x runtime)")
    )
    mem = (mem_bars + mem_points).properties(title="Memory (GB-hours)")
    energy_points = base.mark_point(size=60, color="black", strokeWidth=0.5).encode(
        y=alt.Y("Wh_total"), shape=shape, tooltip=["rule"]
    )
    energy_bars = base.mark_bar().encode(
        y=alt.Y("sum(Wh_dardel_accounting):Q", title="Energy (Wh)")
    )
    energy = (energy_bars + energy_points).properties(title="Energy")
    return (
        alt.hconcat(runtime, eff, mem, energy)
        .configure_axis(labelFontSize=12, titleFontSize=14)
        .configure_legend(labelFontSize=12)
    )
```

## Overview {.smaller}

_NBIS Bioinformatics support project_

**Aim**: Investigate and characterize host-microbiome niches in mouse and human gut

**Support needed**


* Develop [robust]{.green} and [scalable]{.green} analysis pipeline(s) for host and microbial data
* Ensure [reproducibility]{.green}, [computational efficiency]{.green} and [broad usability]{.green}

**Concerns**

* Runtime for 1 sample between 2-11 days.

## Pipeline overview {.smaller}

* Workflow manager: Snakemake
* Software management: pixi/apptainer
* Installation: `pixi shell`

## Pipeline overview {.smaller}

![](../../assets/images/snakevision_dag.svg)

## Optimizations {.smaller}

::: {.incremental}

1. Incorporate bash scripts into Snakemake
2. Remove redundant resource-intensive steps (_e.g._ multiple mapping against host genome)
3. Split input to parallelize taxonomic assignment
4. Optimized python packages (_e.g._ [polars](https://pola.rs/)) instead of custom perl scripts.

:::

## Benchmarking {.smaller}

**Test data**

| sample | total seqs |
|----------------|------------|
| 1.0.1 | 5.5 M |
| 1.0.2 | 11 M |
| 1.0.3 | 16.5 M |

**Pipeline versions**

* `legacy`: original pipeline at start of project
* `updated`: pipeline with optimizations and improvements at end of project

**Compute system**

* [Dardel HPC system](https://www.pdc.kth.se/hpc-services/computing-systems/dardel-hpc-system/) with SLURM workload manager

## Benchmarking {.smaller}

* Snakemake benchmark files for all rules to get runtime, memory usage and CPU efficiency

```{.python}
rule trim_R2:
    benchmark: "results/{sample}/trim_R2.benchmark.txt"
```

* Energy use estimated with:

$$
E_{CPU} = runtime * CPUs * W_{CPU} * PUE
$$

$$
E_{MEM} = runtime * RAM_{peak} * W_{MEM} * PUE
$$

$$
E_{TOTAL} = E_{CPU} + E_{MEM}
$$


* **PUE**: Power usage effectiveness. Data center energy overhead (cooling etc.)
* **W~CPU~**: Watts per CPU.
* **W~MEM~**: Watts per GB RAM.


## Assumptions

* Allocations on Dardel: Peak RAM also allocates CPUs so a job running 1 CPU at high RAM reserves more CPUs.
* Power usage effectiveness: 1.15
* Watts per CPU: 3.5
* Watts per GB RAM: 0.3725

```{python}
#| label: read-data
df = pl.read_csv("../../data/energy_rows.csv")
df = df.with_columns(GB_hours=(pl.col("s") / 3600) * (pl.col("max_rss") / 1000))
df = df.with_columns(max_rss_gb=pl.col("max_rss") / 1000)
df = df.with_columns(thread_eff=pl.col("busy_cores") / pl.col("threads"))
```

## Results

## Preprocessing {.smaller}

```{python}
#| label: fig-preprocessing
#| fig-cap: Runtime, memory and energy usage for read trimming and filtering.
plot(df, part="preprocessing", shape_legend=False)
```

Take-home:

* Runtime and energy usage decreased by ~90% and ~75%, respectively.
* Memory consumption in `updated` flat with increasing sample size.
* Savings grow with sample size.
* **Primary optimizations**: Removal of extra filtering step.
* **Further optimizations**: Reduce allocated threads.

## Alignment and annotation {.smaller}

```{python}
#| label: fig-align-annotate
#| fig-cap: Metrics for alignment + annotation (host) and demultiplexing

plot(df, part="align-annotate", shape_legend=False)
```

Take-home:

* Speed gain moderate (-11% runtime) but energy reduction is large (-84%).
* **Primary optimizations**: 
  * 1 single alignment instead of 2
  * large jobs split into sub-parts with better resource allocation
* **Further optimizations**: Reduce allocated threads for demultiplexing.

## UMI filtering

```{python}
#| label: fig-umi-filter
#| fig-cap: Metrics for UMI filtering

plot(df, part="umi-filter", shape_legend=False)
```

Take-home:

* Runtime and energy usage reduced by ~70%.
* Memory footprint grows faster with sample size in `legacy`.
* **Primary optimizations**: switching from single-threaded looping over every read (legacy) to multi-threaded operations on columns (updated). 
* **Further optimizations**: Reduce allocated threads.

## Taxonomy {.smaller}

```{python}
#| label: fig-taxonomy
#| fig-cap: Taxonomic assignments
plot(df, part="taxonomy", shape_legend=False)
```

Take-home:

* Runtime down 23%, energy down 49%.
* Energy saving grows with sample size (primarily due to lower memory footprint).
* **Primary optimizations**: 
  * skipping post-processing (calculating best-hit, LCA, adding taxonomy).
  * increased parallelization 
* **Further optimizations**: Increase size of splits to reduce overhead.


## Summary {.smaller}

```{python}
#| label: fig-diff
#| fig-cap: Difference in energy usage (updated-legacy) per pipeline part.

agg = df.group_by("pipeline_part", "version", "sample").agg(
    pl.sum("Wh_dardel_accounting"),
    pl.sum("Wh_total"),
)
legacy = agg.filter(pl.col("version") == "legacy")
update = agg.filter(pl.col("version") == "updated")
source = (
    update.join(legacy, on=["sample", "pipeline_part"])
    .with_columns(
        (pl.col("Wh_dardel_accounting") - pl.col("Wh_dardel_accounting_right")).alias(
            "Total (Dardel accounting)"
        ),
        (pl.col("Wh_total") - pl.col("Wh_total_right")).alias("Total"),
    )
    .select("sample", "Total (Dardel accounting)", "Total", "pipeline_part")
    .unpivot(
        index=["sample", "pipeline_part"], variable_name="variable", value_name="W"
    )
)
alt.Chart(source.filter(pl.col("pipeline_part") != "vsearch")).mark_bar().encode(
    x="sample",
    y="W",
    xOffset="variable",
    color=alt.Color("variable").scale(scheme="paired"),
    column=alt.Column(
        "pipeline_part",
        sort=["preprocessing", "align-annotate", "umi-filter", "taxonomy"],
        title="Energy difference by part",
    ),
    tooltip=["W", "variable"],
).resolve_scale(y="independent").configure_axis(
    labelFontSize=12, titleFontSize=14
).configure_legend(labelFontSize=12).configure_header(
    labelFontSize=12, titleFontSize=14
)
```

## Total walltime

Total walltime for test samples per pipeline version.

| version | runtime (s) | runtime (h:m:s) | runtime |
|---------|-------------|-----------------|---------|
| legacy | 150164 | 41:42:44 | 1 day, 17 h, 42 m, 44 s |

* The [updated pipeline]{.green} had a [runtime of 6%]{.green} compared to the legacy version.

## Take-home message

::: {.incremental}
1. Use a workflow manager (helps with parallelization, resource handling, re-runs etc.)
2. Think carefully about workflow structure (minimize redundancies).
3. When possible, split big jobs into smaller steps to use resources more efficiently.
4. Split input files by size to increase parallelization and make resource use predictable (but optimize split sizes).
5. Use built-in post-processing for efficient software (_e.g_ `mmseqs easy-search`) rather than custom-built scripts.
6. Avoid for loops over large data-frames -> instead use purpose-built packages (_e.g._ `polars`).

:::
